doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Computer programming background and work in recording technology
summary: He describes programming business software, then using technology as a producer, engineer and Pro Tools and Internet recording user.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Did we have something we wanted to add over there? Because we can slide this in there.
What is this? I can’t read this.

That was going to bring me back to my question, thank you. Right. Okay. I know you had this computer experience and knowledge all this time. Has it come back to resurface in your life and help you out?
Yeah, it’s been there for a while. It’s funny, since I started, I got a scholarship for mathematics which involved me into computers. For a while as a hobby I did

programming. Some time back I programmed software for businesses. I wrote programs for a book store or a cosmetics company or a public relations firm to name two or three. And I enjoyed it, because I was good at it. But as the technology advanced and the languages advanced I started teaching myself other languages of course, in order to do this. But I realized that the languages started moving pretty fast and if I was going to continue with this I need to go back to school and get back deep into it, and that was taking a lot of time away from music so I decided not to do that. And I became a user, but a very savvy user. And I decided to use it in music. And as a result I’ve been involved in the recording aspects, the new digital recordings. Also I’m a producer and I have produced records both in the audiophile world, I don’t know if you know what that is, and then the multi-tracking, the normal way of recording. So I’m versed in the technology and the way that audiophiles perceive and do things, as well as the digital world of Pro Tools, and I work Rocket Network which is, I’m now involved in an Internet recording situation. So I’m involved with him. I work with E-magic, that company which is software for audio and midi music production, and I work with some music instrument makers like Korg synthesizer makers, Korg and people like that. So I’m involved in that kind of work, I produce, I’m an engineer, I can engineer, and I know all the technical stuff. I’m involved in all of that. So as a producer, because I enjoy being in the studio and producing other artists as well as myself, but other artists, and so you need to have that kind of knowledge.
Well it doesn’t sound like you’re being left behind in the world of technology in all aspects.

No. I like to look forward. I think looking forward is a good thing. You try not to lose certain values that have, in the past have shown to be real truthful things that last. You know, things that are real. Because those are important values. But you need to learn how to take those things with an eye to the future, and keep innovating and continuing to add to it. That’s what I try to do.
